correctness.rationale: Starting from the published independent-parent representation, every two-component labeling is counted by within-block increasing attachments and root choices; averaging the initial run yields the displayed finite mass. Combining with the independently proved Poisson-binomial root law normalizes the result. Exact arithmetic exhausts all parent assignments through n=7 and verifies normalization to n=100. Uniform weight asymptotics and harmonic normalization prove the unrestricted log-scale limit; finite checks are not relied on for the limit.

originality.rationale: The founding author-open preprint, arXiv:1906.08806, expressly identifies the full exchangeable partition probability function as lacking a closed expression; only the root-count and unconditioned selected-tree laws are supplied. Later arXiv:2509.19678 studies edit-chain spectra, not partition sizes. Specific searches for the Moran two-block sector and the log-uniform conditioned law returned no coincident or stronger result. Residual risk of unindexed equivalent work is acknowledged, not treated as proof of historical priority.
residual_risks: Indexed search and the inspected papers do not exhaust all unpublished manuscripts, theses, older books and translated equivalent results.
General all-block EPPF literature might contain an unindexed special case of the two-block formula; no such decisive source was identified.
The asymptotic conditional law cannot be inferred from the marginal component-count distribution; a future independent literature review may identify alternative proofs.

value.rationale: The EPPF is the natural, expressly identified unresolved descriptor of the stationary Moran forest. Its exact complete two-component sector is nontrivial at every finite order and yields a qualitative rare-event phenomenon: conditioned on exactly two components, the smaller component has no single deterministic power scale, with a uniform logarithmic exponent. This is not the ordinary typical-tree size law, and can serve as a baseline for later multiblock EPPF investigations.
